findings.title: Server compressor factory mutated cross-shard, causing unsynchronized UB
findings.claim: server_factory lives on shard 0 but loopback_socket_impl::connect round-robins server connections, so at default --smp 2 the stream connection's negotiate() runs const_cast<...>(this)->hooks.push_back(...) on shard 1 against a shard-0 vector — unsynchronized mutation with a buffer allocated by shard 1's allocator and freed by shard 0, which is UB that ASan/UBSan won't catch.

findings.title: Test hardcodes hooks.size()==2/hooks.back() ordering and captures auto& into growing vector
findings.claim: hooks.size() == 2 plus hooks.back() hardcodes loopback's shard/ordering policy, and capturing auto& into a growing std::vector is invalidated by any later negotiation.

findings.title: Commits and PR body carry Claude authorship trailers/attribution lines
findings.claim: All three commits carry Co-Authored-By: Claude trailers (4 lines across f545c28a, 5e25ebdb, 69da8f5b), and the PR body has the "🤖 Generated with Claude Code" line; both should be stripped.

findings.title: put(std::span<temporary_buffer<char>>) override breaks builds at --api-level=7|8
findings.claim: The put(std::span<temporary_buffer<char>>) override only exists at SEASTAR_API_LEVEL >= 9 (guarded by an #if in loopback_socket.hh:144), which breaks --api-level=7|8 even though CMakeLists.txt:72 still accepts those levels.

findings.title: Test never asserts the send was refused; success case is silently swallowed
findings.claim: The test never asserts the send was refused; catch (closed_error&) {} swallows the success case too, so a regression that accepted-and-dropped the frame would still pass. The throw should be asserted.

findings.title: Commit documents sink/source but omits send_empty_frame
findings.claim: Commit 3 documents sink and source but not send_empty_frame, the one API whose failure mode this PR widens.

findings.title: Re-entry into stream_close() guarded only by error(), not by _stream_closing
findings.claim: Re-entry into stream_close() is guarded only by error(), which is false for the whole new await; reachability is low (needs source::make_sink() re-open) and the issue is pre-existing, but adding !error() && !_stream_closing is free.

findings.title: Drain wait is unbounded and its comment doesn't name what breaks it
findings.claim: The drain wait is unbounded; the comment would be more useful naming what breaks it (stop_send_loop's shutdown_output) rather than only who no longer waits. Not a regression.

findings.title: Inner lambda parameter f shadows outer auto f
findings.claim: The inner lambda param f shadows the auto f from line 549, in the statement assigning the outer one.

findings.title: Doc overstates that both halves of a stream must always be closed
findings.claim: "Both halves of a stream must be closed" overstates it; with no returned sink, _source_closed is true from construction (rpc.hh:301), so the doc should say "each half you were given".

findings.title: Ternary data.size ? ... : snd_buf(...) is a no-op copied from a neighbour
findings.claim: The data.size ? … : snd_buf(...) ternary is a no-op that appears to have been copied from a neighbouring test.

findings.title: for (i < 10) yield() loop uses an unexplained magic constant
findings.claim: The for (i < 10) yield() loop uses a magic constant of 10.

findings.title: New comments use two spaces after a full stop, inconsistent with rest of file
findings.claim: New comments use two spaces after a full stop; both files use one space everywhere else.

findings.title: stream_close() could previously close output_stream while a queued send_entry() was mid-write/flush
findings.claim: The drain wait added by this PR incidentally removes a second, previously unclaimed bug: stream_close() could close the output_stream while a queued send_entry() was mid-write()/flush() on it.
